name: CMN Hypha
synopsis: The reference CMN client CLI — release spores, query synapses, resolve bonds, and manage your local mycelium.
intent: Provide the reference CMN client: release signed spore manifests, query Synapse indexers for discovery, resolve bond URIs, verify content hashes, and manage the local development workflow
Enable any developer to publish, discover, and consume spores from the command line — the primary interface for interacting with the CMN network
mutations: Rebuild the command-line boundary on agent-first-data's closed-world CLI registry — every executable argument combination is registered up front, help is emitted as cli-help-v2, and docs/cli.md is rendered by the binary itself via --docs; clap is gone. Unregistered argument mixtures fail before any config, filesystem, network, or domain I/O, and repeatable options such as --exclude-names bind one value per occurrence where clap accepted a variadic list

Own the whole command lifecycle with a single AFDATA emitter on a dedicated writer thread, so protocol ordering, stream routing, and the single-terminal-event rule hold across the thread-safe EventSink trait
Redact credential-bearing values before they reach protocol events — scrub scheme-prefixed URLs embedded in diagnostic prose, and secret-named fields inside embedded CMN documents
Edit hypha config through the agent-first-data document API so unrelated file content and formatting survive a write, and report load and parse failures as structured errors

Accept nutrient fields the mycelium model does not name — mycelium nutrient add --with stores unrecognized keys as parsed JSON, so a spec-valid BOLT12 offer or a new payment network needs no hypha release

bonds.reason: Implements the CMN protocol specification — reference client CLI
All CLI output and protocol fields use Agent-First Data suffix conventions
